problem: Existing EIF planners either need supervised training on labeled ALFRED trajectories or LLM in-context examples (LLM-Planner needs ~100 annotated samples), and most lack re-planning grounded in visual observations (LLM-Planner only uses visible object lists).
motivation: EIF needs long-horizon compositional planning, and labeled data is costly and generalizes poorly to unseen instructions and environments. Zero-shot LLM planning is hard for complex tasks, and failures at execution need visual understanding of the scene to be corrected.
key_idea: Let the LLM decompose an instruction via self-generated question-and-answer about 'things to discover' (sub-tasks, order, objects, execution methods) to produce subgoals zero-shot, and use an MLLM's visual QA to diagnose failures and re-plan.
insight: Explicit self-QA decomposition is what drives the gains: removing STD drops valid-unseen Subgoal ACC from 43.36 to 25.94 and SR from 14.62 to 9.00, and replacing it with zero-shot CoT is even worse (23.39 ACC), since CoT extracts information haphazardly. Gains are largest on long-horizon tasks (Clean +61.95, Cool +58.72, Heat +23.53 Subgoal ACC), while tasks violating common-sense simulator constraints (Pick Two, Stack) remain hard without in-context examples.
method: Socratic Task Decomposer (STD): prompts the LLM with its role, sub-task explanations, simulator rules and 'things to discover' (sub-tasks, ordering, target objects, execution methods) so it generates its own QA conversation about the instruction, zero-shot.

Task Planner: takes the instruction and QA conversation plus simulator rules and output format, and produces a list of subgoals (action, object[, receptacle]) compatible with the HLSM low-level controller.

Vision-based Socratic Re-planning (VSR): on subgoal failure, an MLLM is asked whether the subgoal is valid in the current scene; if the target is not among the observed objects or the subgoal is invalid, it generates feedback QA (failure cause, corrective action).

Re-plan/retry decision: if the target object is visible and the action seems valid, failure is attributed to the controller and the subgoal is retried; otherwise the Task Planner revises the plan from the feedback, observed object set and validity, and execution resumes.
RelaxedHLP metric: high-level plan accuracy metric that accepts multiple valid plans (temporally agnostic, spatially agnostic, interchangeable subgoal order).
Integration: uses HLSM's low-level controller and object detector, same as the LLM-Planner baseline; the prompts are simulator-agnostic apart from the sub-task explanations and object space.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o for LLM/MLLM in the method description; the appendix says GPT-3.5-Turbo (LLM) and BLIP-2 flan-t5-xl (VLM) were used; HLSM low-level controller and detector (all frozen prompting)
setting.training_data: none (training-free, zero-shot prompting); the HLSM controller is pre-trained separately
setting.observation: egocentric RGB image (plus detected object list from HLSM perception); RGB-D on the real robot
setting.action_space: high-level subgoals (action, object[, receptacle]) executed by HLSM low-level controller; UR5e Pickup/Put/Open/Close/Push in the real world
setting.simulator: AI2-THOR (ALFRED) plus a real UR5e tabletop

results: In the zero-shot setting, Socratic Planner beats the few-shot LLM-Planner (9 examples) on all metrics; e.g. valid-unseen SR 15.35 / GC 29.20 vs 12.92 / 25.35. It stays far below the fully supervised CAPEAM (test unseen SR 43.69). On the real robot it reaches 53.3 SR and 81.7 Subgoal ACC vs 46.7 / 61.7 for LLM-Planner.
limitations: Gains in high-level plan accuracy do not fully translate into task SR, because the HLSM low-level controller often fails (wrong detections, distance) and failures accumulate under the 10-failure limit.
Weak on Pick Two and Stack tasks, since the simulator's constraint of not holding two objects conflicts with common-sense plans that zero-shot prompting cannot know.
Absolute SR remains low compared to fully supervised methods; the real-world experiment is small and human-judged.
